Duress

dur-ESS · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Duress is threats, force, or other harsh pressure used to compel someone to act against their will.

The union argued that workers had only accepted the pay cut under duress, threatened with immediate layoffs otherwise.

Worked Example

During the trial, the witness explained that he had only signed the false statement under duress, after being threatened with harm to his family.

The witness didn't sign willingly -- he was forced through fear and threats. That state of being pressured or coerced into an action is exactly what duress means.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

coercion: the use of force or threats to make someone do something

compulsion: a strong pressure or force driving someone's action

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

consent: free and voluntary agreement to do something

free will: the ability to choose and act without being forced

Where it sits · how harshly a person is forced — pressure → duress → torture

pressure vs. duress: Pressure can be mild, like a deadline or a parent's nagging, far short of actual threats or force.

torture vs. duress: Torture involves inflicting severe physical or psychological pain, a far more extreme and violent form of coercion than duress usually implies.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — dur-

root — dur-: hard (Latin (durus))

suffix — -ess

suffix — -ess: the quality of (French -esse) (French)

Put it together

Put it together: Duress comes from Latin durus ('hard') plus -ess, the French noun ending -esse meaning 'the quality of' -- so duress is literally 'hardness.' Something done under duress is done under hard, harsh pressure, forced rather than freely chosen.

Use the root in a new word: endure

Use the root in a new word: endure: The climbers had to endure three days of freezing temperatures before reaching base camp.

Word Choice

Duress is a formal, often legal word -- you'll hear it in courtrooms and contracts ('signed under duress') far more often than in everyday conversation.
